title: kv-cache: memory defrag + spillover eviction heuristics v10 to reduce fragmentation and paging churn
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and spillover paging have been a recurring source of tail latency and higher GPU memory churn for mixed-size inference workloads. Previous heuristics reduced average spillover but left pathological fragmentation cases where lots of small KV entries prevented large contiguous allocations, triggering repeated paging and defrag cycles. This PR introduces a multi-pronged set of improvements (v10): 1) compacting allocator pass that opportunistically coalesces free spans during low-util periods, 2) hot/cold classification for KV entries that biases eviction and spillover toward cold, high-fragmentation candidates, 3) a lightweight background sampler to detect fragmentation hotspots and preemptively schedule targeted defrag windows, and 4) improved integration with the scheduler so defrag work is placed on spare worker slots and avoids interfering with low-latency requests. Changes are additive and guarded by a runtime flag; default behavior is enabled for Dedicated/Demo infra and can be toggled for Hosted via feature rollout. Benchmarks: internal perf bench shows ~18% reduction in 99th-percentile token latency for mixed-chat workloads and ~12% lower GPU memory reclaim overhead on long-running sessions. The description below summarizes commits, changed areas, CI, and review notes.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Overall looks solid. Can we avoid an O(N) scan on every allocation? Suggest we limit compaction to a budget per defrag window.
Priya Nair: Addressed - added per-window budget and adaptive backoff (see allocator.cc lines ~210-260). Added unit tests that assert budget limits.
Sofia Martinez: The hot/cold classifier seems to treat small keys as cold which may cause eviction storms for many small active keys. Can you add an lru-window check?
Priya Nair: Good catch. Added LRU-window threshold and hysteresis to prevent thrash. See eviction_policy.cc and new tests. Also instrumented classifier metrics (kv.hot_ratio, kv.cold_evictions).
Liam O'Connor: Defrag runs should not coincide with peak serving windows. How is scheduler integration preventing this?

Priya Nair: Defrag scheduler now consults worker idle score and the new 'defrag_safety_margin' configured per deployment. Default margin is 20% spare capacity. If margin not met, defrag is deferred. Added integration tests and adjusted docs.

SRE Bot: perf benchmark flagged a 3% reg on tail in one synthetic microbenchmark; author confirmed this was within noise and provided additional long-run numbers showing improvement. CI perf run passed on rerun.
Ethan Park: Approved after fixes and added telemetry.
ci_checks: perf-bench: passed (bench1: -18% p99, bench2: -6% avg, synthetic micro run flakey but re-run passed)
release_notes:
- Improved KV cache memory management: compacting allocator reduces fragmentation and contiguous allocation failures.
- Hot/cold classification for KV entries to bias spillover/eviction away from hot entries, reducing paging churn.
- Background fragmentation sampler and scheduler-aware defrag windows to avoid interfering with low-latency requests.
- New metrics: kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.defrag_cycles, kv.hot_ratio.
- Rollout: feature-gated and enabled by default for Dedicated; opt-in for Hosted via feature flag.
notes: This PR is intended to be low-risk: all new behaviors are behind runtime flags and have conservative defaults. Perf harness and long-run nightly measures included in the perf workflow. Follow-ups: explore GPU-side pinned allocations to further reduce paging and a subsequent v11 to tune eviction weights per model family.
